title: Adversus Valentinianos
author: Tertullian
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0275.stoa008.opp-lat1, as held by the Perseus Digital Library.

passages.original: Nec undique dicemur ipsi nobis finxisse materias, quas tot iam viri sanctitate et praestantia insignes, nec solum nostri antecessores, sed ipsorum haeresiarcharum contemporales, instructissimis voluminibus et prodiderunt et retuderunt, ut Iustinus, philosophus et martyr, ut Miltiades, ecclesiarum sophista, ut Irenaeus, omnium doctrinarum curiosissimus explorator, ut Proculus noster, virginis senectae et Christianae eloquentiae dignitas, quos in omni opere fidei, quemadmodum in isto, optaverim assequi. Aut s(??)in totum haereses non sunt, ut qui eas pellunt finxisse credantur, mentietur apostolus praedicator illarum.
passages.english: Nor shall we be said on any side to have invented for ourselves the subject matter, which so many men distinguished for holiness and excellence, not only our predecessors but contemporaries of the heresiarchs themselves, have both made public and refuted in most learned volumes: such as Justin, philosopher and martyr; Miltiades, the sophist of the churches; Irenaeus, the most careful investigator of all doctrines; and our own Proculus, the glory of chaste old age and of Christian eloquence, whom I would wish to match in every work of faith, as in this one. Or if heresies do not exist at all, so that those who drive them out are believed to have invented them, the apostle who foretold them will be lying.
passages.notes: "s(??)" is a damaged form, evidently "si" ("if"). "Virginis senectae" is taken as "chaste (virgin) old age"; the phrase is unusual.

passages.original: Primus omnium Ennius, poeta Romanus, Coenacula maxima caeli, simpliciter pronuntiavit, elati situs nomine, vel quia Iovem illic epulantem legerat apud Homerum. Sed haeretici quantas supernitates supernitatum, et quantas sublimitates sublimitatum in habitaculum dei sui cuiusque suspenderint, extulerint, expanderint, mirum est. Etiam creatori nostro Enniana coenacula in aedicularum disposita sunt forma, aliis atque aliis pergulis superstructis et unicuique deo per totidem scalas distributis quot haereses fuerint.
passages.english: First of all Ennius, the Roman poet, simply declared "the greatest upper rooms of heaven", using the term for an elevated position, or because he had read in Homer of Jupiter feasting there. But it is astonishing how many heights upon heights, and how many loftinesses upon loftinesses, the heretics have hung up, raised and spread out as the dwelling of each one's god. Even for our Creator, Ennius' upper rooms have been arranged in the form of small apartments, with storey after storey built on top, and allotted to each god by as many staircases as there have been heresies.
passages.notes: "Coenacula" denotes upper rooms or garret apartments in a tenement block; the image is of a Roman apartment building.

passages.original: Itaque omnes forma et scientia peraequantur, facti omnes quod unusquisque; nemo aliud, quia alteri omnes. Refunduntur in Nus omnes, in Homines, in Theletos, aeque feminae, in Sigas, in Zoas, in Ecclesias, in Fortunatas, ut Ovidius Metamorphoses suas delevisset, si hodie maiorem cognovisset. Exinde refecti sunt, et constabiliti sunt, et in requiem ex veritate compositi magno cum gaudii fructu hymnis patrem concinunt.
passages.english: And so they are all made fully equal in form and knowledge, all become what each one is; none is anything different, because all are the others. They are all poured back into Nous-es, into Anthropoi, into Theletoi, likewise the females, into Sigai, into Zoai, into Ecclesiai, into Fortunatae, so that Ovid would have erased his Metamorphoses if he had known today a greater one. After that they were restored and established, and, set in rest by the truth, with great enjoyment of joy they sing hymns together to the Father.
passages.notes: The plurals are of Valentinian aeon names: Nous (Mind), Anthropos (Man), Theletos (Desired), Sige (Silence), Zoe (Life), Ecclesia (Church); "Fortunatas" probably renders Makaria (Blessedness). "Ex veritate" may mean "truly" rather than "by the truth".
